seoTitle: Engine and aircraft sourcing and sales support | Flight Hour Solution
metaDescription: Engine and aircraft sourcing and sales support from Zug, Switzerland, with the broker role disclosed in writing. Recent listings and a request form.
title: Engine and aircraft sourcing and sales support
intro: Our Assets line finds engines and aircraft for people who need them and markets them for owners. When we broker, we say so.
disclosure: Assets is a separate line from Advisory, our consulting line. When we act as a broker on an engine or aircraft, we say so in writing before you rely on our view of it. Advisory clients are never offered an asset we represent without that disclosure. Flight Hour Solution is not owned by an MRO, a lessor or an OEM.

howItWorks.title: Tell us what you have or need
howItWorks.text: Use the form below or write to us. For an engine: type and variant, thrust rating, time and cycles since new and since the last shop visit, LLP status, location and preservation state. For an aircraft: type, MSN, engine status, lease or sale, and when you need it.
howItWorks.source: Listing fields from docs/research/07-recommendations-and-brief.md section 5 (Assets brief: model, ESN status, cycles and time remaining, location, availability date).

howItWorks.title: We state our role in writing
howItWorks.text: Before anything else, you learn which party we act for, whether we hold a mandate on the asset, and on what terms. That note goes on file. Advisory clients receive the same disclosure before any asset is put in front of them.
howItWorks.source: Conflicts policy from docs/research/07-recommendations-and-brief.md section 2.3 option 1 (when we broker an asset we say so; advisory clients are never sold our own inventory without disclosure).
clientToConfirm: Confirm that the role statement will be issued in writing on every Assets engagement and that it names the terms of remuneration.

howItWorks.title: We search, or we list
howItWorks.text: For a wanted asset we approach owners, lessors and operators directly. For an offered asset we prepare a specification sheet from the records and circulate it to our contacts and on our LinkedIn page.
howItWorks.source: LinkedIn as the channel used for offers and requests: docs/research/01-company-profile.md section 3 (timeline of offers and requests) and section 4.3.
clientToConfirm: Confirm whether the owner's name is withheld from the specification sheet until a serious enquiry arrives. No confidentiality practice is stated on the page until confirmed.
Confirm whether part-out specialists are approached for wanted assets. They are not named on the page because the research does not document it.

howItWorks.title: We check the records, not just the price
howItWorks.text: For the buyer or lessee we act for, we read the asset the way we read an engine before a shop visit: back-to-birth trace of the life-limited parts, the last shop visit report, borescope video, AD and SB status, and remaining time and cycles against the price asked. You get a written view before you commit.
howItWorks.source: Review items from the company's own service taxonomy in docs/research/02-website-content-inventory.md section 4 (LLP back to birth trace audit, technical documentation audit, borescope video analysis, engine evaluation and selection).
clientToConfirm: Confirm that a written technical view is part of every buy-side Assets engagement, and what it covers (records, borescope video, AD and SB status, test cell or on-wing run data).

howItWorks.title: Negotiation, paperwork and handover
howItWorks.text: We support the purchase or lease negotiation and check the delivery documentation against the agreed condition. If the engine is heading for a shop visit next, our Advisory line can take over from there, on a separate engagement.
howItWorks.source: Engine purchase negotiation, lease contract negotiation and documentation audit: docs/research/02-website-content-inventory.md section 4. Separation of the two lines: docs/research/07-recommendations-and-brief.md section 2.3.
clientToConfirm: Confirm whether the company follows the asset to physical acceptance (engine stand, preservation, shipping, records pack). This is not claimed on the page because the research documents it only as competitor vocabulary (05 section 4).

requestForm.title: Request or offer an asset
requestForm.text: Listings above appeared on our LinkedIn page and may no longer be open. Tell us what you are looking for or what you are selling.

fields.name: assetModel
fields.label: Engine or aircraft type
fields.hint: For example CFM56-7B26, Trent 772B, PT6A or Boeing 737-800.

fields.name: message
fields.label: Message
fields.hint: Time and cycles since new and since the last shop visit, LLP status, location and timing help us answer faster.

requestForm.notes: Field set from the page brief (name, company, email, asset type, engine or aircraft type, need offered or wanted, message). The options and hint keys follow the FormField type in site/app/src/site/types.ts and the contact.json field shape, so the same form component can render this form. The route currently renders EnquiryForm with contact.form; to use these fields the component needs the assetType and assetModel keys added to its field list and to its mailto builder, and its validation currently requires a message regardless of the required flag here. Consent text, submit label and success copy are shared with the contact form and live in contact.json.

notes: Assets is the second of the two labelled lines under one brand (07 section 2.3 option 1); Advisory is described on the services pages and the independence statement on the About page. recentActivity is a record of what the company has publicly offered or sought, newest first, not a live availability list: every item comes from a dated LinkedIn company post recorded in 01 section 3, and the completed Trent sale of 5 March 2026 is left out because the table types are offered and wanted only. Dates are ISO 8601 so the mono date column sorts and reads unambiguously for an international audience. No market figures are used on this page. The route hides the activity table when the array is empty, so items can be removed once the client confirms they have been placed. sales@flighthoursolution.com is not rendered anywhere pending confirmation (see clientToConfirm). The form has no file upload; borescope reports and records can follow by email after first contact.

sales@flighthoursolution.com is used on LinkedIn for asset enquiries (01 sections 4.3 and 6). Confirm whether it may be published on this page and whether the request form should deliver to it rather than to contact@flighthoursolution.com.

Confirm the status of each item in recentActivity (sold, placed, withdrawn or still available) and the LinkedIn dates recorded in 01 section 3, and supply the fields for a live listing if one is wanted at launch: model, ESN, status, time and cycles remaining, location, availability date (07 section 5).

A completed Rolls-Royce Trent engine sale was announced on LinkedIn on 5 March 2026 (01 section 3). It is omitted because the table shows offered and wanted items only. Confirm whether completed transactions may be shown, and with what detail (variant, buyer type, whether the company acted as broker or seller).

Trent 772B and PT6A fall outside the engine families listed on the Services page (CFM56, LEAP, V2500, PW4000, Honeywell APU and turboprop). Confirm whether Assets covers any type or a defined list, and whether that list should be stated on this page.

The Aviation Suppliers Association membership and the AircraftParts hashtag point to parts supply (01 section 4.3). Confirm whether parts or modules should be an asset type on the form; it currently offers Engine, Aircraft and Other. 06 section 5.2 advises against presenting the firm as a parts supplier, so no parts activity is described.

07 section 5 proposes availability alerts by subscription for the Assets page. None is included because no mailing tool, consent text or retention rule exists yet. Confirm whether to add one at launch or in phase 2.
